title: Coastal Wave Processing and Directional Light Painting in Photoshop (PNW 1-3, Part 6 - 2024)

date.basis: embedded_creation_time metadata; transcript does not independently confirm the shooting date

summary: This instructional portrait of coastal editing walks through a photographer-editor's workflow to elevate a shoreline image. It covers selecting suitable waves and light across multiple frames, cropping for sky, and building directional sunset-like lighting through staged local dodging and color grading. The process includes raw adjustments, shadow/highlight manipulation, and a blend of two shots via clone-stamping techniques, followed by selective color work, an HDR-like texture boost, perspective corrections to the horizon, and final refinements to rocks, water, and sky. The narrative emphasizes maintaining natural looking light while shaping depth through controlled, zone-by-zone adjustments and cautious use of HDR texture on the water.

sections.title: Initial global adjustments to expand dynamic range
sections.description: Open with intent to expand the dynamic range while keeping shadows dark; establishes baseline processing context.

sections.title: Wave and light source scouting across shots
sections.description: The editor evaluates the current file for a near-perfect wave and second wave; considers blending a shot with waves between rocks but notes focus issues and light availability.

sections.title: Camera-movement consequences for blending feasibility
sections.description: Discussion of whether blending could work given different compositions and focal lengths; emphasizes lack of alignment between shots.

sections.title: Determining blending feasibility across frames
sections.description: Conclusion that blending light across shots is not feasible due to the absence of matching light in alternative takes.

sections.title: Strategic cropping and shot selection for later processing
sections.description: Notes on potential cropping later to include more sky; evaluation of prior options and decision to focus on a single shot with strong potential.

sections.title: Sky/light trade-off and plan to render strong light
sections.description: Acknowledge epic skies came with reduced light; reframing the task as creating light where it was missing rather than waiting for ideal conditions.

sections.title: Directing light with wide framing and pre-visualization
sections.description: Guidance to go wide early to ensure sky data is captured, anticipating later cropping decisions.

sections.title: Shadow dodge build-out for directional light
sections.description: First pass of shaping light by brightening a defined area to invite directional light and then applying targeted dodging to allocate light paths.

sections.title: Fine-tuning wave lighting and color with selective targeting
sections.description: Shade the wave with whites and color grade to create a sunset feel; paint light onto the wave and other breaking waves; emphasize directionality while preserving edges.

sections.title: Foreground rock and rock-texture stabilization
sections.description: Addresss color inconsistencies in foreground rocks, adding sunset hues and raising dynamic range in problematic zones to achieve cohesion.

sections.title: Increasing light bleed and RAW-based refinements
sections.description: Introduce more directional light, perform highlight dodge in controlled steps, revisit RAW to push warmth, and introduce an HDR-like texture boost to enhance surface detail in water.

sections.title: Before/after remix and horizon framing
sections.description: Demonstrates remaking the light by blending adjustments gradually; compares before and after and adjusts horizon emphasis through selective remasking.

sections.title: Horizon correction with perspective tools
sections.description: Uses perspective-based correction to straighten the horizon, preserving the rebalanced tonal relationships.

sections.title: Final color, texture, and detail refinements; seagull embellishment
sections.description: Concludes with layered color work (clouds and sky hues) using 50-150 adjustments, targeted selective color on rocks and sky, final horizon and wave tweaks, and a closing note about adding a seagull to complete the composition.

featured_techniques.technique: Shadow Dodge to sculpt directional light
Highlight Dodge to simulate light catching surfaces
Selective Color for localized color control
Auto HDR (tone-mapped HDR) texture boost in RAW
Remix light across the scene via staged intensity
